newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 25.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Manila Archbishop Jaime Cardinal Sin warns of another "people power" rally if the Ramos government pursues its plan to amend the Constitution, even as President Fidel Ramos says he is willing to let the charter change take place after the 1998 elections (ALL PAPERS)
- Some 300 "Edsa babies" will join the whole-day programme commemorating the 11th anniversary of the 1986 EDSA uprising (PHILIPINE DIALY INQUIRER)
- Senator Heherson Alvarez sends Senator Nikki Coseteng two dozen yellow roses to apologise for the glass throwing incident which marred their closed door hearings (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- The National Telecommunications Commission further cut the proposed fees for the use of the frequency spectrum of existing carriers. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- The national government posted a budget deficit of nearly 3.4 billion pesos last month. (ALL PAPERS)
- The debts of Philippine Phosphate Fertiliser Corp ballooned to 40 billion pesos by the end of last year, the parent National Development Co says. (BUSINESS STAR)
